safi-cedvel:1-5.t:
* I'rab:
(بربّ) is attached to (أعوذ). (من شرّ) is attached to (أعوذ) in all four places. (ما) is a relative noun in the position of genitive, as muḍāf ilayhi [Note: or a maṣdar particle, with الخلق meaning "the created" or meaning "origination" ... said by al-ʿUkbarī.], and the returning pronoun is omitted. (إذا) is an adverb in the position of accusative, stripped of the conditional sense, attached to the maṣdar (شرّ غاسق). (في العقد) is attached to (النفّاثات). (إذا) is like the first, attached to the maṣdar (شر حاسد)..
Clause: «قل ... » has no grammatical position; it is inceptive.
And the clause: «أعوذ ... » is in the position of accusative, the thing said.
And the clause: «خلق ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (ما).
And the clause: «وقب ... » is in the position of genitive, as muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «حسد ... » is in the position of genitive, as muḍāf ilayhi.

* Morphology:
(1) الفلق: a noun meaning the dawn [Note: the exegeses give many meanings for al-falaq, among them: a prison in Hell, or a valley in it, or low-lying ground, or the womb ... etc.]; its wazn is فعل with two fatḥas.
(3) غاسق: an active participle from the triliteral غسق, i.e. "became dark"; its wazn is فاعل, and it is the night [Note: or it is the moon when it darkens or is eclipsed, or the sun when it sets, or the snake when it bites, or every attacker that harms ... etc.].
(4) النفّاثات: plural of النفّاثة, the feminine of النفّاث, an intensive form of the active participle, i.e. women who blow on knots for sorcery; taken from the triliteral نفث (class of نصر and class of ضرب); its wazn is فعّال.
(5) حاسد: an active participle from the triliteral حسد; its wazn is فاعل.

* Benefits:
- Envy (ḥasad) and emulation (ghibṭa):
Ḥasad is wishing for the removal of a blessing from another, and that is blameworthy. The Jews, may Allah curse them, used to envy the Prophet for the Qur'an and the blessing of Islam sent down to him. As for ḥasad, if its meaning is rivalry and competition in good deeds, this is praiseworthy, for the noble ḥadīth which says: "There is no envy except in two: a man whom Allah has given wealth and empowered to spend it on what is right, and a man whom Allah has given knowledge which he teaches to people." As for ghibṭa, it is that you wish to become like the possessor of the blessing, without wishing its removal from him, and this is not blameworthy.
